newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA STOCKS END LOWER, THIRDLINERS STEAL FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: MANILA STOCKS END LOWER, THIRDLINERS STEAL FOCUS.

text.p: Manila shares fell on Friday as the consolidation mode persisted with buying concentrated on tertiary issues while blue chips were mostly sold, traders said.
The composite index broke through its 2,650 support but closed off its intra-day low of 2,635.34 points. The market gauge finally settled 22.19 points lower, or 0.83 percent, at 2,647.82.

"People were taking profits after eight days of straight gains. Besides there are still uncertainties in the currency market and the nationwide transport strike did not help sentiment," said Henry Ong, analyst at Sapphire Securities.
Transport groups launched a nationwide strike on Friday to oppose the recent increases in petroleum product prices.
The most heavily traded issue was Republic Resources and Development Co which rose 18 centavos, or nine percent to 2.18 pesos.
Other actively traded thirdliner issues which registered gains were Picop Resources and Liberty Telecommunications Holdings Inc.
Traders said a technical bounce in Meralco B shares towards close of trading tempered the market's losses.

"The speculative stocks are keeping the market alive. This consolidation will continue until perhaps interest rates go down further or until the end of the third quarter," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Equities Inc.
All indices closed lower except for the commercial-industrial sub-index which posted a slight rise.
Turnover was slightly improved at 2.07 billion pesos from the previous day's 1.93 billion. Decliners exceeded gainers 75 to 40 with 58 issues unchanged.
